The Delibru reusable cups for Keurig brewers have a "shower head" design and lots of screen area, including the bottom. In fact, there's so much screen, and so little plastic frame, that it feels flimsy. The bottom screen is recessed to prevent it from being punctured by the Keurig's bottom piercing needle (good) but that method of protecting it also reduces the volume for coffee, thereby limiting brew strength significantly. Because the side screen extends almost to the lid, a portion of the incoming water bypasses most of the coffee grounds, further weakening the brew. I tried various grinds (including fine) trying to find the sweet spot. But I was never able to make decent coffee except at the Keurig's smallest cup size.

I stopped using these and tried a competing product by ValueCafe (6-pack for $7.99 on Amazon), which is apparently a very new design. It's very sturdy, has a protected bottom screen. a real hinge for the lid, and is also a "shower head" design. I was very pleased with the ValueCafe product (see review)). It's so new the picture on the box did not correspond to the product (but the web page pictures did) and there were no instructions on the box or enclosed with the product. Hopefully, ValueCafe will fix those issues quickly.

Running, the unit draws 108W (as measured with a "Kill-A-Watt" meter)
Over a 10 day test period, my unit consumed 6.34 kWh. That's 0.63 kWh per day (11 cents worth of power where I live).

Works like a champ, but I recommend these procedures and considerations. If you expect to unpack the Igloo 103 and in 10 minutes have enough ice for a party, this ain't for you.
First, unpack, place on the level surface on which the little guy will do his stuff, and let it set until tomorrow (next day). The manual says let it set 10 hours.
Second (next day), after you untape the ice bucket and scoop, rinse them with hot water then dry. Also, wipe out the interior with a damp multi layer paper towel.
Third, fill a gallon jug with filtered water and pour into the water chamber to just below the max fill line (won't use the entire gallon).
Fourth, install the ice bucket and close the lid.
Fifth, plug in and let it go to work.
When you press start, the machine defaults to medium size ice cubes. I recommend you leave it at this setting until you've let the machine run for about three (3) hours. You may discover "medium" is the perfect size.
On the first operation, expect the first ice in about 20 minutes. Don't expect the first few ice drops to be useful. The ice maker will start dropping cubes about every 10 minutes or so. It takes about two hours to get the ice to the correct size and have enough to fill a large glass. At three hours, you'll have enough ice for, maybe, three large glasses or four or five smaller glasses. This gadget is strictly for family use and small gatherings.
